interest: This document illustrates the administrative tracking and diplomatic management of United States Government property located in enemy territory (Japan) during the height of World War II through a neutral protecting power (Switzerland). It reveals how local municipal and fiscal obligations, specifically land and real estate taxes on American property in Yokohama, were still formally addressed and communicated via the Swiss Foreign Office in 1944. Furthermore, it provides researchers with an important archival cross-reference (SEE: 125.9911/326) to trace the underlying diplomatic notes and records concerning the wartime status and maintenance of American consular or government holdings in Japan.
overview: This file consists of a single Department of State List of Papers sheet (Form DS-46) dated October 12, 1945, cataloguing correspondence filed under decimal classification 894.5122, which pertains to Japanese land and real estate taxation. The document records a single entry (Sub No. 2) referencing communication #7725 dated March 30, 1944, received from the Swiss Foreign Office acting as the neutral protecting power during World War II. The entry concerns a note regarding the payment of local taxes on United States Government-owned real property in Yokohama, Japan, and directs researchers to cross-reference file 125.9911/326.

subfiles.about: A Department of State index sheet listing an entry regarding Japanese land and real estate taxes on U.S. Government property in Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: This State Department List of Papers (Form DS-46), dated October 12, 1945, indexes documents filed under subject heading 894.5122 (Land Tax / Real Estate Tax -- Japan). It catalogs Sub No. 2, an enclosure transmitted by Switzerland (#7725) dated March 30, 1944, containing a note from the Swiss Foreign Office regarding the payment of taxes on U.S. Government property in Yokohama. The entry indicates that the original document was transferred or filed under decimal classification 125.9911/326.
